title: An 800-Pound Beast and a Fire That Killed a Scout Troop: Two Wisconsin Roads Made the Most Haunted in America List
excerpt: Two Wisconsin roads made a national top 10 list of the most haunted roads in the US. Meet the Beast of Bray Road and the legend of Boy Scout Lane.
content:
It's spooky season which means it's time for... scary stories. I mean, scary stories are good any time of year, but tis the season.

There are two roads in Wisconsin that were recently named some of the most haunted roads in the entire country by Discover Cars. Have you visited these places? Do you believe these stories? Let's find out.

ALSO READ: Zumbrota Haunt Shuts Off Every Light and Gives You One Candle

The first Wisconsin road that made the '10 Most Haunted Roads in the US' list, is Bray Road in Elkhorn.

The story is that there's a creature called the Beast of Bray Road and this has been the tale since the 80s. It's described as "a massive 800-pound, six-to-seven-foot-tall beast covered in dark fur, complete with glowing red or orange eyes."

Witnesses say the Beast has scratched cars, and others say they just see it lurking in the shadows. People have also said they see it running on two legs.

The Beast of Bray Road is so well-known that it's been featured in a 2005 movie all about it (called 'The Beast of Bray Road'), a 2018 documentary called The Bray Road Beast, and has been featured in several shows.

The Most Haunted Roads in Wisconsin - Boy Scout Lane

The second Wisconsin road featured is Boy Scout Lane in Linwood (near Stevens Point).

The story says that a Boy Scout troop was camping in the area in the 50s or 60s when they were killed in a fire. Some versions of the story say the Scoutmaster did it and others say the bus driver who took them to their campsite did it.

Either way, today, people claim to see shadowy figures in the trees, some say they hear footsteps, and others report "an unnerving feeling of being watched".
